# Nuthatch

> A self-hosted-first, AI-native blockchain indexer in one Rust binary. From a contract
> address to a live indexed API, with no mandatory third-party data service and nothing
> phoning home.

Nuthatch indexes EVM chains on your own hardware. Embedded mode runs as a single static
binary with no external services: no Postgres, no Docker, no IPFS. It is free and licensed
MIT OR Apache-2.0. Status: **v3.8.5**. Stability is a promise, not a claim of completeness: no
CLI flag, HTTP route, config key or generated column is renamed or removed without a major bump, and
upgrading stays a binary swap with no data migration. This file separates what the binary does today
from the design targets, so a model does not present unbuilt features as present-tense fact.

Tagline: "Be your own indexer."

## What it does today

- `nuthatch init 0xAddr [0xAddr…] [--chain <mainnet|arbitrum-one|base|bsc|polygon|gnosis|optimism>]`
  resolves each contract's
  ABI (Sourcify, then an Etherscan-class API; EIP-1967/legacy-OZ proxies resolved) and scaffolds a
  multi-contract nest: `nuthatch.toml`, `abis/`, a `schema.json`, a `semantic.toml` (per-nest
  meaning, seeded from the ABI), a commented `views/` starter, an `llms.txt`, and a Claude Code
  skill. Omit `--chain` and nuthatch probes each supported chain for the contract's bytecode. It
  does not yet auto-generate the view logic, handlers, or tests from the ABI.
- `nuthatch sql "…"` runs one-shot SQL from the terminal (aligned table, `--json` to pipe), or opens
  an interactive REPL (`.tables`/`.schema`, history) when given no query. `nuthatch add 0xAddr` grows
  a nest with another contract without re-init. `nuthatch mcp --print-config` prints a copy-paste MCP
  client config; systemd/docker recipes run `dev` unattended.
- Governed semantic layer (RFC-0016): the `semantic.toml` drives an enriched `schema` (meaning +
  hot/cold coverage seam + derived footguns); a failed query returns a one-line fix hint and `explain`
  validates a query without executing it; MCP results are compact tables with a citable provenance
  stamp (`as of block N, sealed_through M, registry <hash>`).
- `nuthatch dev` polls logs over RPC (round-robin failover, adaptive `getLogs` chunking), decodes
  every declared event of every contract (topic0 registry → one table per `{alias}__{event}`),
  including an empty typed table before a declared event has fired,
  stores rows in an embedded hot store (redb), seals finalized ranges to content-addressed Parquet
  (hot store pruned), and serves a local HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:8288: `/tables`, `/table/{name}`
  (hot+cold merged), `/schema` (the enriched data model), `/sql` (read-only DuckDB, sealed history
  UNION the live hot tip), `/explain` (validate SQL without running it), `/entity/{id}`, `/balances`,
  `/balance/{addr}`, `/exposure/{addr}`, `/flags`, `/ready` (readiness: 200 fresh / 503 stalled),
  `/metrics` (Prometheus), and a localhost-gated admin UI at `/_admin/`. Every row carries provenance columns (`block_hash`, `_seq`,
  `block_timestamp`) and `*_dec`/`*_overflow` siblings for big integers.
- A nest is a git repo: `nuthatch init --from <git-url | ./dir>` runs a published nest (vendored
  ABIs + deployment blocks, schema-version guarded); authored `views/*.sql` (RFC-0018) are a
  validated, drift-gated layer - each binds against the schema at load, so a moved column is a loud
  `nuthatch check` failure, described in `semantic.toml` and surfaced in `/schema`; `nuthatch check`
  also runs `checks/*.sql` against recorded fixtures (hermetic parity/invariant framework).
- Authored incremental entities (RFC-0041, stable in 3.0.0): an `entities.toml` declaration points
  to one `SELECT`, its unique key and `max_rows`. Nuthatch maintains that bounded relation as blocks
  arrive, retracts it on reorg, exposes it on `/sql` and `/derived/{entity}`, and reports its
  applied-through watermark plus six per-entity Prometheus series. Views remain query-time SQL. An
  entity seeds from locally stored history on restart and `dev --seal-direct` refuses a nest that
  declares one rather than serving an empty result.
- Balances are an incrementally-maintained view (DBSP): i128 base units serialised as decimal
  strings, a reorg is a retraction, and the view replays from stored facts on restart.
- `dev --seal-direct` writes finalized history straight to Parquet, bypassing the hot store, while
  producing byte-identical segments and resolving every declared `[[calls]]` input. The former
  ~8.7x seal-direct and ~20x stacked speedup claims were withdrawn in 2.7.0 after a harness fix made
  their denominator invalid; a deterministic replay rig comes before another multiplier. Operator
  surface: `/metrics`, `/ready`, `/sql` guards
  (30 s timeout, 50,000-row cap, 64 MiB result-byte ceiling, 2 concurrent, a filesystem-access
  denylist, and single-statement enforcement - a `;`-stacked statement is refused), health-aware RPC
  failover (a failing endpoint is benched on a cooldown), startup segment recovery (hash-verify +
  quarantine), graceful shutdown on SIGTERM.
- `nuthatch transform <component.wasm>` runs a pure, zero-capability WASM transform over an Arrow
  batch. `nuthatch mcp` serves the Model Context Protocol over stdio (12 tools: status, schema,
  tables, table, sql, explain, entity, balance, top_balances, flags, exposure, screen_status; plus 3
  resources - nuthatch://schema|tables|status - and 3 prompts: profile-contract, investigate-address,
  verify-a-number), bridging offline to a running instance.
- Factories and dynamic contract discovery (RFC-0009): `[[templates]]`/`[[factories]]` index the
  child contracts a factory deploys at runtime (it indexes Uniswap), tip + backfill + reorg-safe,
  with a `{template}__children` view.
- Compliance pack (RFC-0008): sanctions screening against content-addressed list snapshots
  (`nuthatch screen`, replayable `sanction_hit` annotations), threshold/velocity flags at `/flags`,
  counterparty exposure at `/exposure/{addr}`, alert webhooks via a durable at-least-once outbox, and
  a signed pack manifest (`pack build`/`verify`, ed25519) with `audit replay`/`report`.
- Admin UI and webhooks (RFC-0010): an embedded read-only admin UI at `/_admin/` (no framework/CDN,
  localhost-gated), plus user `[[webhooks]]` that POST sealed rows matching a `where` clause,
  HMAC-signed with `X-Nuthatch-Signature`.
- Nest packaging and multi-nest tenancy (RFC-0012 + RFC-0032, complete): `nuthatch nest bundle`/`load`
  build and verify a content-addressed, portable nest `.bundle` (loadable from a file or an http(s)
  URL), reproducing the decode registry from the installed inputs. **There is no `roost` subcommand -
  it was removed in 2.0, not renamed.** One `nuthatch dev --dir <dir>` runs one nest or many
  depending on what the directory holds: a `nuthatch.toml` or a `mounts.toml`. A nest's data is keyed
  by its content address (`data/<nid>/`) and a mount is keyed by `(tenant, nid)`, so two mounts may
  share one dataset and it is never indexed twice; unmounting one of two decrements a reference
  rather than destroying data someone else is using, and `nuthatch prune` reclaims what nothing
  mounts any more. `nuthatch migrate` moves a pre-2.0 directory across. A tenant is an opaque
  ownership label - no identity, no authentication, no quotas, no metering. Verified live on Arbitrum.
- The nest registry (RFC-0019): publish and pull nests by `name@version` from a filesystem or S3
  backend; versions are content-addressed, so what you resolved is what you run.
- Safe upgrades, no resync tax (RFC-0020): `nest diff` classifies an update as compatible or
  breaking; `nest upgrade` hot-swaps a compatible one with an atomic endpoint flip after the new
  version catches up (reusing the old sealed segments when decode is unchanged, so it costs seconds
  rather than days), and serves a breaking one at a new endpoint with RFC-8594 deprecation headers on
  the old.
- Multichain runtimes (RFC-0021): one runtime hosting nests across more than one chain via
  `[[chains]]` in `mounts.toml`, with one isolated cursor per chain (its own tip, finality, and reorg
  boundary) and a per-cursor footprint budget. Multichain is a capability, not a mandate - one chain
  per runtime stays valid and is the default, and a cursor is never multiplexed across two chains.
- Derive-first contract reads (RFC-0023, tiers 1-3): `nuthatch recipe add total_supply|balances|
  holder_count|reserves` derives what a subgraph pays an archive node to `eth_call` for, from the
  events already indexed - no archive node, no eth_call. `nuthatch metadata fetch` calls once and
  caches the immutable reads (`decimals`/`symbol`/`name`). Tier 3 (2.6.0) is the escape hatch when a
  value genuinely cannot be derived: a `[[calls]]` block reads contract state via `eth_call` **pinned
  to a fixed block**, so the result is reproducible rather than whatever the chain says today. A
  `[[calls]]` block is either sampled (one fixed calldata every N blocks) or row-driven (RFC-0038 §3:
  one call per row of a table at that row's block, arguments taken from the row's columns - what a
  mapping's `balanceOf(event.params.to)` does). Since 2.7.0 the streaming and every seal-direct path
  resolve these reads; the benchmark does so in both
  arms and requires `--state-rpc` rather than silently skipping them.
- Adaptive MCP tool advertisement (RFC-0025): `GET /shape` reports which capabilities a nest can
  actually answer, and the MCP bridge filters `tools/list`/`prompts/list` accordingly, so an agent is
  never handed an inert tool. Fails open if the probe fails.
- Fault quarantine and partial health (RFC-0026): a faulting nest is quarantined rather than fatal -
  healthy siblings keep indexing and serving, and a retryable fault is re-admitted on a backoff. A
  nest's error no longer kills its cursor and a cursor's death no longer kills the runtime. Surfaced
  by `GET /nests` (live per-nest health merged per request), runtime-root and per-nest `/ready`, and the
  `nuthatch_nest_health` / `nuthatch_nest_quarantine_total` / `nuthatch_cursor_live` metrics.
  `--fail-fast` restores exit-on-first-fault for CI.
- Publishing sealed segments (RFC-0052, 3.7.0): `nuthatch publish sync --target <dir |
  s3://bucket/prefix>` mirrors every segment that is not provisional to `<target>/<data identity>/`;
  `publish verify` checks each object against the local catalogue (`--deep` re-downloads and
  re-hashes; `--etag-md5` compares ETags on a store whose ETag is the object's MD5), and `publish
  status` reports what is still to upload and writes nothing. `dev` and `serve` mirror continuously
  with `--publish-target`, `--publish-interval` and `--publish-parallelism`, on their own thread, so a
  slow bucket delays the mirror and never a seal. Credentials are the usual `AWS_*` variables. A
  published prefix is plain Parquet plus a catalogue; CI checks Trino against DuckDB over one.
- `nuthatch emit dune --dir <nest> --out <dir> --source <namespace>` (RFC-0055, 3.7.0) writes one plain
  DuneSQL `SELECT` per event table over `dune.<namespace>.<table>`, offline and deterministically,
  keeping every wide integer's exact text beside it as `<name>_raw`. The queries do not by themselves
  put data in Dune; `--source` names the namespace the rows were uploaded into. Since 3.8.3 it also
  writes a query for each authored view whose DuneSQL translation is exact, and lists every other view
  under "Not emitted" with the construct that stopped it.
- IPFS documents at scale (RFC-0037 slices 5 to 8, 3.8.0): `[[ipfs]]` takes `cid_json_path` and
  `json_match` to read a CID out of JSON in an event column or a top-level call's calldata. Every
  document resolves behind the cursor with retry and a recorded give-up, and sealing holds below any
  block whose documents are still undecided. A multi-block document is proven against its CID, and an
  unproven one writes no row. `[ipfs.rows]` explodes a proven JSON document into typed rows in its own
  table; `keep_content = false` drops the raw JSON. Documents given up on are listed at
  `GET /ipfs/gave-up` (3.8.2), and under `--seal-direct` one document holds a window for at most
  `--ipfs-window-deadline` (300 s by default). A seal cut is bounded at 20,000 rows or 64 MiB of row
  JSON, whichever comes first.
- Store coverage check (3.8.4): a nest records its chain, each contract's address and start block, its
  factories and its extraction settings in the store, and refuses to start a store holding data if
  `nuthatch.toml` has since changed any of them. RPC endpoints and the nest's name may change freely.
  `/` and `/nest` show the nest's `nid` and `data_identity`.
- Chains: Ethereum mainnet, Arbitrum One (42161), Base (8453), BSC (56), Polygon (137), Gnosis (100)
  and Optimism (10) are built in, with keyless public endpoints, a tuned `eth_getLogs` window, and
  finality as a per-chain policy. **Any other EVM chain
  also works** by supplying `chain_id` + `rpc_urls` by hand (`dev`, `sql`, `bench`, `serve` are
  chain-agnostic; `init`/`add` are not, since ABI resolution is chain-gated) - an unlisted chain
  inherits depth-64 finality and a 20-block window, and its `chain_id` is verified against every
  endpoint at startup. The bundled free public RPCs exist so `init` → `dev` works with zero setup;
  they are rate-limited, shared, and unsuitable for deep backfills or production - use your own node
  or a paid provider for real work. Measured footprint: ~37 MB single contract, ~58 MB three-contract
  23-table nest (2.8% of the 2 GB per-cursor budget; CI fails above 256 MB).

- **Scaffolding a nest from a subgraph manifest**: `nuthatch init --from-subgraph <CID|url>` maps
  `dataSources` -> `[[contracts]]` and `templates` -> `[[templates]]`, vendors every ABI from the CID the
  manifest pins, carries `startBlock` across, and carries each dataSource's `eventHandlers` over as that
  contract's event allowlist. The pinned ABIs beat Sourcify for proxy-heavy codebases, where Sourcify
  returns the proxy ABI that declares none of the events the contract emits. Factory rules are inferred
  only where a parameter unambiguously names a template - which template a factory creates lives in the
  mapping WASM, not the manifest, so anything ambiguous is reported with candidates rather than guessed.
  A CID names what to ask a gateway for, and an `[[ipfs]]` block (RFC-0037) resolves documents and
  **verifies the returned bytes against the content address that names them**, so a lying gateway is
  caught rather than indexed. Between `[[calls]]` and `[[ipfs]]`, the two things a subgraph could do
  and a nest could not are no longer missing, and neither costs the determinism.
- `nuthatch doctor --rpc <url> --address 0xAddr` probes an endpoint and reports the largest `getLogs`
  window it will actually serve, its batch limit, and whether it has archive history - measured
  against that endpoint rather than read from its documentation. With `--dir`, it uses the nest's
  full declared contract set rather than only the first address.
- **Scaled mode** (RFC-0022, opt-in at build time with `--features postgres-store`, so the default
  binary carries no database driver): the same crates run as a control plane holding desired state, a
  writer pool whose members take **one lease per chain cursor**, and an independently-scaled query
  tier. Ownership is enforced by the store - every write carries a fence, and a stalled worker that
  wakes finds its writes refused. Workers **pull the nests they are assigned** from a registry; with a
  `bundle_hash` pinned the fetch is by content address, so re-tagging a version in a registry cannot
  change what a fleet runs. Verified across real machines, including 377 blocks indexed through a
  90-second control-plane outage.
- **Measured performance**: Sentio's OBIB benchmark, case 1 (LBTC `Transfer`, 22.2M Ethereum blocks)
  completes in **74.8 s** for **294,278 events** in **321 RPC requests** at 320 MB peak RSS, against a
  real provider. The event count matches Sentio's own README. `block_timestamp` is demand-driven;
  measured real backfills attributed roughly 80% of provider compute units to header reads, and
  2.7.0 makes partial-batch retry splits descend concurrently. The `getLogs` window adapts to what an
  endpoint will actually serve.

## Design targets (not built yet)

- reth ExEx tip-ingestion against your own node (designed and stubbed; toolchain + dependency
  blockers cleared, needs a synced node; RPC is the working path), and firehose-class extraction of
  traces and state diffs on top of it (RFC-0014, deferred).
- DataFusion federation (RFC-0013 §2). **Decided against for 1.0 on measurement, not preference**:
  the benchmark gate found DataFusion 1.6-2.7x DuckDB's latency on the fold that matters, with the gap
  widening as segments grow, at exact result parity. DuckDB is the engine in both modes. Do not
  describe nuthatch as using DataFusion.

- Streaming subscribe (SSE); local AI models (Ollama /
  bring-your-own-key); effectful HTTP egress for transform worlds (`kv` grant ships today);
  wildcard signature-scoped indexing.
- GraphQL (RFC-0053) is no longer a design target: 3.7.0 ships a partial read surface, exact for a
  subgraph's event-shaped fields and a named refusal for the rest, and it is parked. An analytics
  client cannot adopt it unmodified, because GraphQL refuses a whole query for one unanswerable
  field. Do not describe it as a drop-in replacement.

## How it works

- Ingestion (RPC extraction today; reth ExEx when colocated, designed) -> deterministic decode
  -> a hot store (redb) for point-reads at the tip -> content-addressed Parquet sealed past
  finality -> embedded DuckDB attached read-only for analytical SQL. Balances are declarative
  incremental views (IVM).
- Reorgs touch only the mutable hot store and become retractions in the incremental view. The
  columnar layer is append-only by construction.
- The escape hatch is capability-isolated WASM components via WIT. A component granted zero
  capabilities is a pure function and can be re-executed and verified; its purity is checkable
  from its imports alone.

## Principles

- Single static binary; zero external services in embedded mode.
- No phone-home: no telemetry, no mandatory API tokens, no gated data service, ever.
- Deterministic core: decode, reorg handling, and entity derivation are reproducible. LLMs
  generate code and tests; LLM output never sits in the runtime data path.
- AI-native today: a built-in MCP server, a `schema` tool, and a shipped `llms.txt` and Claude
  Code skill, all offline against your local instance. Local models (Ollama / BYO-key) are planned.

## Install

**v3.8.5 is the current release.** The installer and `cargo` fetch the latest. Two artifacts and two
container images per release: the default (embedded) one, and a `-scaled` one carrying `worker` and
`control`. Images are at `ghcr.io/nightswatchhq/nuthatch` (`:3.8.5`, `:3.8.5-scaled`, `:latest`).

**3.8.0 makes an `[[ipfs]]` nest over megabyte documents fit to deploy.** Every document a nest names
resolves behind the cursor, is proven against its CID however many blocks it spans, and can be
exploded into typed rows (`[ipfs.rows]`); a seal cut is also bounded at 64 MiB of row JSON. It adds
`--cors <ORIGIN>` on `dev` and `serve`, `--explorer <URL>` (a Blockscout instance) on `init` and `add`,
`init --from-subgraph` over a local `subgraph.yaml`, and a `doctor` that finds its own probe address
without `--address`. `/sql` and `/explain` answer `503` when the hot tip holds more than 64 MiB of row
JSON, and a `/sql` request waits up to 250 ms for a free permit before it is refused. An events-only
nest swaps the binary and restarts. A nest that has indexed top-level calls must re-index (call rows
now carry `tx_from`), and a nest with `[extract] traces` gets a new identity. An `[[ipfs]]` name or
`[ipfs.rows]` table declared twice or landing on an event or call table, and a decoded call argument
named `tx_from`, now refuse to start. After one start on 3.8, a nest with `[[calls]]`, `[[ipfs]]` or
`[extract]` is refused by 3.7.0; an events-only nest can go back.

**3.8.1 to 3.8.5 are binary-swap patches.** 3.8.1 checks an empty document body against its CID
instead of retrying it. 3.8.2 logs and counts every retried document fetch
(`nuthatch_nest_ipfs_retries_total`), grows the fetch timeout from 30 to 60 to 120 s, gives a
`--seal-direct` window at most `--ipfs-window-deadline` (300 s) per document, lists documents given up
on at `GET /ipfs/gave-up`, adds three `/ready` fields, and holds a hot-mounted nest to one backfill
window at a time on a single-endpoint chain. 3.8.3 keys a runtime nest's cursor, health and metrics by
its route, so the `nest` label on `nuthatch_nest_*` is the route where it differs from the nest's name,
and `emit dune` translates authored views whose DuneSQL is exact. 3.8.4 records what a store covers as
`indexed_coverage` and refuses to start a store whose chain, contracts, start blocks, factories or
extraction settings no longer match `nuthatch.toml`; the first start after upgrading records rather
than verifies. 3.8.5 fixes a `/sql` panic on scaled `DECIMAL` results too wide for the driver, and
sealed velocity seeds that were silently skipped.

**3.7.0 mirrors sealed segments to a bucket and emits DuneSQL.** `nuthatch publish sync|verify|status`
and `--publish-target` on `dev`/`serve` (RFC-0052); `nuthatch emit dune` (RFC-0055). The DuckDB memory
walls are environment settings with unchanged defaults, new seals are zstd, a declared query
(`/q/{name}`) answers `422` when its plan could read more than 512 MiB, and a local offchain file drop
stores a file as an immutable snapshot. The x402 counter and `nuthatch settle` exist only in a
`--features counter` build; no release binary contains them. A nest with a ported
`graph/schema.graphql` answers GraphQL as a partial read surface, exact or refused by name field by
field, that is parked and is not a drop-in replacement for a subgraph. Most operators swap the binary
and restart. The exceptions: `NUTHATCH_SQL_MAX_CONCURRENCY` above 2 refuses to start unless
`NUTHATCH_ANALYTICS_MEMORY_LIMIT` comes down (256MB at four permits), and a nest with a fully named,
non-indexed tuple event parameter gets a new NID and re-indexes (#1364). Downgrading to 3.6.1 after
running 3.7.0 is not safe.

**3.0.0 makes authored incremental entities stable.** A nest can declare a bounded keyed relation in
`entities.toml`, maintained as blocks arrive and queryable through `/sql` and `/derived`. Existing
nests remain a binary-swap upgrade; adding an entity seeds local history on restart, and
`--seal-direct` refuses an entity-bearing nest. Every release artifact carries a GitHub
build-provenance attestation, verified with `gh attestation verify <tarball> --repo
nightswatchhq/nuthatch`.

**2.7.0 made `[[calls]]` and `--seal-direct` compatible.** It also narrows and retries the factory
fetch for newly discovered children on a provider cap, gives declared-but-unfired events empty typed
tables, repairs stale schema columns from the live registry, probes all contracts in `doctor --dir`,
parallelises timestamp retry splits, and redacts state-RPC credentials from benchmark output. The old
seal-direct multipliers were withdrawn because their baseline came from an obsolete harness path.

Apart from the 3.7.0 and 3.8.0 exceptions above, upgrading is a plain binary swap - on-disk state is forward-readable and the `dev` flags are stable, so
no migration or re-backfill is involved. Minimum supported Rust version is **1.95**.

**Two security patches are worth knowing about if you advise anyone on a version.** Both are on the
`/sql` surface, which binds 127.0.0.1 by default:

- **v0.9.3** fixes an **arbitrary file read**: DuckDB accepts a quoted function name and the guard
  matched only an unquoted one, so `SELECT * FROM "read_csv"('/etc/passwd')` executed. Every earlier
  release is affected.
- **v0.6.2** fixes an **arbitrary file write** via `;`-stacked `COPY ... TO`.

Earlier milestones: 0.9 brought scaled mode's writer pool and the backfill work above; 0.8 the
control plane; 0.7 the live roost and the relicense to `MIT OR Apache-2.0`; 0.6 nest bundles, the
registry, and zero-downtime N-1 upgrades.

- Prebuilt binaries for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux x86_64 on the GitHub release, with
  SHA-256 checksums; the one-line installer (`curl -fsSL https://nuthatch-indexer.com/install.sh | sh`)
  downloads and verifies them.
- `cargo +1.95.0 install --git https://github.com/nightswatchhq/nuthatch nuthatch` (**exactly 1.95.0** - `rust-toolchain.toml` does not apply to `cargo install`, and 1.97 hits a dbsp ICE).
- A Homebrew tap and detached release signatures are still on the way. The OCI image ships today.

## Worked example

`/example` indexes USDC on Ethereum mainnet from its contract address: `init` vendors the ABI and
scaffolds the nest, `nuthatch dev` backfills and follows the tip, every declared event becomes a table
(`usdc__transfer`) queryable through read-only SQL over HTTP and MCP, and the page then chooses
between an authored view and a maintained entity. It is the current, executable path on v3.8.5.

## Who runs it

`/stories` answers "is this for me?" through three illustrative personas (not testimonials),
each mapped to one of the three front doors: an SQL endpoint for application backends, published
nests for analysts who write no indexing code, and the built-in MCP server for agents. These
workflows run on v3.8.5 - multi-contract nests, every declared event as a table, seven built-in
chains, user-authored views, maintained `entities.toml` relations, `init --from`, `/sql`, and MCP all
ship, as do factories, the compliance pack, the admin UI, and webhooks. GraphQL is not one of the
front doors: the read surface shipped in 3.7.0 is partial and parked. It notes that derived views read finalized data while raw event
tables are fresh to the tip.

## Roadmap

`/roadmap` is generated from the source repo, not from marketing copy: the README's working-now
table and progress log are the source of truth for what is shipped, and the numbered RFCs under
`docs/rfcs/` for what is planned. Shipped: the embedded pipeline end to end, nests, seven built-in
chains (Ethereum mainnet, Arbitrum One, Base, BSC, Polygon, Gnosis, Optimism), the correctness-gated
seal-direct and pipelined backfill paths (RFC-0004), the operator surface (`/metrics`, `/sql` guards, graceful
shutdown), factory/dynamic discovery (RFC-0009, it indexes Uniswap), the compliance pack (RFC-0008:
screening, flags, exposure, signed audit), a local admin UI + webhooks (RFC-0010), content-addressed
nest packaging (RFC-0012), the delightful core (RFC-0015: sql/REPL, magical init, add, prod
recipes), the governed semantic layer + agent-grade MCP (RFC-0016/0017), the nest registry
(RFC-0019), N-1 upgrades (RFC-0020), multichain runtimes (RFC-0021), derive-first recipes and pinned
`eth_call` (RFC-0023 tiers 1-3), adaptive MCP tools (RFC-0025), fault quarantine (RFC-0026), live
mount and unmount with no co-tenant restart (RFC-0027), `eth_getLogs` range-control hardening
(RFC-0028), the tenant runtime that retired the roost and keyed nest data by content address
(RFC-0032), identity and grafting (RFC-0033), the query allowlist (RFC-0034), calldata decode and
the `[extract]` surface (RFC-0014 slice 0 - decode, schemas and volume guard; extraction itself
still needs a colocated node), verified IPFS resolution (RFC-0037), subgraph-manifest scaffolding
(RFC-0038), distributed scaled mode (RFC-0022 - a control plane, a writer pool taking cursor
leases, and an independently-scaled query-FE tier), sealed segments mirrored to a bucket (RFC-0052),
DuneSQL queries emitted for a nest (RFC-0055), and proven, typed IPFS documents at scale (RFC-0037
slices 5 to 8). v3.8.5 is the current release, with prebuilt
binaries and container images - one embedded, one `-scaled`.

**The 2026 feature freeze is over.** It ran from 2026-08-20 to 2026-09-08 and was lifted in full. The
work since is the RFC-0044 to RFC-0048 programme (the subgraph port, offchain data, x402 at the
counter, the lakehouse commitments, pricing query access), plus RFC-0053, RFC-0052 and RFC-0055.
Deferred items stay deferred and reopen one at a time (`docs/frozen-for-2027.md` in the nuthatch
repo): reth ExEx wiring (RFC-0003, needs a synced node), the remaining release engineering (RFC-0005:
signing, Homebrew), firehose-class *extraction* (RFC-0014, needs the node), IVM generalisation, and
wildcard indexing.
Not planned: a token or decentralized-network features, telemetry, a Kubernetes-first deployment,
and any gateway/auth/metering layer in the core. It promises order, not dates, and defers to the
README progress log when the two disagree.
